proposals.title: One Throw vs. The Loop
proposals.logline: At TritonGym, two athletes write code on a sheet of paper and fold it into a paper-plane "kernel" for the same operator event. Cocky One-shot gets a single throw and CLANGs into the compile gate. Little Evo turns every failure into feedback (compile gate, then the referee's reference check, then the stopwatch), refolds, and on its 4th of 5 allowed attempts its emerald dart beats the hand-tuned golden oracle plane home: Perf@1 > 1.

cast.name: Flash (the One-shot athlete)
cast.concept: The One-shot workflow: a single pass and the lower bound. He is the slow-baseline running gag, like the picture book's snail. After one throw he is benched, and he reacts in every later shot.
cast.design: A tall coral capsule body (h 2.2, r 0.35) with the head as the capsule's top. He wears a cream torus sweatband with two long ribbon tails (thin extruded strips on a sine flutter) and a flat cream bib on the chest with an inked "1". Limbs are thin tapered noodle tubes with ball hands; feet are flattened cream capsule sneakers. The face is 2D ink tracked to 3D: dot eyes and one cocky brow line, with a mouth only on takes (smirk, jaw-drop). Acting: snappy and over-confident. He is all flourish and no care, and deflates vertically like a punctured balloon when he fails.
cast.silhouette: A tall, skinny exclamation mark with ribbons streaming off the head, the tallest shape in the cast.

cast.name: Evo (the iterating athlete)
cast.concept: The iterative-refinement workflow (AlphaEvolve-style): evaluator feedback, up to 5 attempts. Its punch card with 5 holes is the attempt counter, and one hole is still open at the end.
cast.design: An emerald #059669 sphere body (r 0.7) with a slight squash, stubby cylinder legs with round feet and short tube arms with mitten hands. It wears a cream visor cap (a flat cylinder plus a crescent bill) with a hexagonal pencil (cylinder plus cone tip) tucked in it. A cream rounded-rectangle punch card with 5 inked circles hangs on a lanyard at its belly, and a hole pops through (a real 3D cut-out) each time it throws. The face is two tall oval ink eyes, plus a tongue-tip of concentration and a mouth only on takes. Acting: earnest, precise and bouncy. It gives a small overshoot nod when it learns something, and gets star eyes at the payoff.
cast.silhouette: A round ball with a visor bill jutting out and a card dangling below: short and wide next to Flash's tall and thin.

cast.name: The Oracle (the champion)
cast.concept: The hand-tuned oracle Triton kernel that every generated kernel is timed against. Its golden plane is the oracle kernel, and it always lands inside the reference outline.
cast.design: A brass/ochre trophy chalice: a lathe-built bowl body on a short stem, with a disc base that it glides and hops on. Two torus loop handles are its arms, with small ball hands. It wears an emerald leaf-extrusion laurel wreath on the rim and carries a brass-foil paper plane. The face is half-lidded slit eyes (smug), with a mouth only for the final jaw-drop. Acting: languid swagger. It buffs its plane and knuckles, throws with a lazy flick, and at the end its laurel slides over one eye.
cast.silhouette: A chalice with two ear-like loop handles and a wreath crown.

cast.name: Clank (the compile gate)
cast.concept: The standardised compile tool. The portcullis slams on a kernel that does not compile and lifts for one that does, and it spits failures back as feedback.
cast.design: An arch spanning the launch lanes: two thick cream stone cylinder pillars with emerald rivet studs and a half-torus lintel. A portcullis of 7 ink-black iron cylinder bars drops on a spring. The face sits on the lintel keystone: dot eyes (dozing slits at rest) and a gritted-teeth mouth only on the CLANG. The bars sag and lift with its breathing.
cast.silhouette: A wide arch with vertical bars, the only doorway shape in the set.

cast.name: Ref (the verifier)
cast.concept: The verify tool: it checks the landed result against the PyTorch reference, drawn as an inked reference outline on each landing pad, and needs max abs error <= 0.01 for Pass@1. It also clicks the profiling stopwatch and hands back the feedback.
cast.design: A short, stout cylinder with ink-black and cream horizontal stripes, a tiny flat cap with a bill and a coral whistle on a cord. It carries an oversized magnifier (torus rim plus a refractive-looking cream disc, flat-shaded) and a flag that swaps between coral-red and emerald-green. Dot eyes; one eye swells huge behind the lens. Acting: fussy and exact. It waddles, bends deep to inspect and snaps flags with an overshoot flutter.
cast.silhouette: A squat striped can with a big round lens held out to one side.

proposals.world:
One continuous three.js set: a sports gym built on a giant GPU card, rendered through the comic NPR (cel ramp, boiling ink, halftone, off-register print, paper grain) on warm cream paper.

- The hub is a raised square emerald chip-die platform (about 10x6 units) with rows of gold pins along its edges (about 40 small cylinders). It sits on a darker-emerald PCB board with raised gold trace lines.
- At the back of the board, a big two-fan cooler housing with 7-blade fans turns continuously (72 frames per revolution, so it loops). Heat-sink fins stand as 6 to 8 slab bleachers. Behind everything is a cream paper cyclorama with halftone clouds.
- The launch line is a chalk line at the hub centre, with a small stool holding a paper stack. The three athletes stand on a diagonal: Evo front-centre (the hero), Flash back-left, the Oracle back-right.
- Clank's arch straddles the lanes about 3.5 units to the right. The planes fly out through it (+x) and follow a closed CatmullRom circuit. The circuit banks round behind the hub and the scoring arch, sweeps past the spinning fan and over the heat-sink fins, and comes back in from the left.
- The planes land on two low cream landing pads to the left of the athletes, each with a thick inked plane-shaped reference outline. Ref stands between the pads.
- The scoring arch at the back-centre has two pillars and a beam:
  - The beam carries a cloth banner hand-lettered "TritonGym", the only appearance of the name.
  - A big brass stopwatch sits on the left pillar top, above the pads. It has a cream dial and two hands: a gold hand for the oracle and an emerald hand for Evo.
  - Low on the right pillar is a chunky rolodex event deck: operator cards with small glyphs (a dot-grid-times-grid for matmul), with "164" painted on its base.
  - The payoff letters hang hidden inside the beam on springy cords.
- Flash's bench and towel sit at the hub's front-left corner.
- The home camera is a low 3/4 medium-wide (about pos (-1.5, 3.2, 10.5), looking at (0.3, 1.3, -0.5), fov 32). Faces sit in rows 600-830, the stations in the central band and the banner in rows 190-280. Nothing important goes near the top-right LIVE pill.
- Palette:
  - Emerald dominant: the hub, Evo, the laurel and the payoff letters.
  - Coral as the single pop colour: Flash, the red flag, the feedback ink and the whistle.
  - The Oracle and the stopwatch are brass/ochre, kept as a warm neutral like the comic reference's ochre.
  - Ink black on cream.
- The paper planes are big: roughly Evo's body width. Each is a 6-vertex folded dart in cream paper with ink code squiggles. The final dart gets an emerald stripe; the Oracle's plane is brass foil. A crumpled plane is a noise-displaced icosphere.

beats.shot: B1 Line-up: low 3/4 medium-wide of the launch line on the chip-die hub. The lane runs right to Clank's arch; the TritonGym banner and scoring arch are behind, the fan spins back-left.
