Evo scribbles carefully, tongue-tip out. f24-47: Evo holds its punch card up to camera (five open holes) with a proud nod, overshooting down and back. f48-71: the Oracle huffs on its golden plane and buffs it, half-lidded. Clank dozes with its bars sagging and lifting as it breathes. Ref twirls its whistle by the landing pads.
beats.concept: One operator event of the benchmark. Every workflow gets the same standardised stations (compile gate, verify pads with the reference outline, profiling stopwatch) and faces the same hand-tuned oracle. Bib "1" means a single pass; five holes mean up to 5 attempts.
beats.camera: A continuous slow push-in and descent carried over from B8, drifting right. It ends on the athletes with Clank entering frame right.
beats.transition_out: Continuous camera move: the push turns into a truck right as both athletes wind up.

beats.shot: B2 CLANG: low chase from just behind the athletes, trucking to a medium on Clank's arch.
beats.action: f72-83: Evo punches hole 1 (a click shake of the card). Both snap-spin their sheets into planes in 6 frames. f84-95: anticipation, both crouch with arms cocked (squash). f96-101: release. Flash throws an overhand whip without even looking and Evo does a two-handed push; bodies stretch. f102-113: the two planes wobble toward the arch and Clank's eyes snap open. f114-119: the bars SLAM down with a hand-lettered "CLANG!", a 2-frame black/cream impact frame and a shake. Both planes accordion-crumple against the bars. f120-143: Clank grits its teeth. In the background the Oracle lifts its nose with a sniff.
beats.concept: Compile: the standardised compile tool stops a kernel that doesn't compile. Both workflows' first try fails the same way, so the start is fair and the workflow is what differs next.
beats.camera: Truck right with the planes (fov 34 to 30), with an 8 degree dutch tilt and a 6% punch-in on the CLANG, then settle.
beats.transition_out: Whip pan left with smear: Clank's bars spring and flick both crumpled balls back toward the start, and the camera whips with them.

beats.shot: B3 One throw vs. a note: medium two-shot at the launch line, Flash left and Evo right.
beats.action: f144-155: Flash's ball bonks his head (squash). He pats his pockets and reaches for the paper stack. f156-171: Ref's whistle toots and it points at his bib "1". f172-191: Flash deflates about 20% vertically, trudges to the bench and flops the towel over his head. Staggered 8 frames behind: Evo catches its ball and uncrumples it to find one squiggle circled in coral ink. Its eyes widen with a small "!". It rubs out the squiggle and rewrites it (f176-195). f196-207: Evo refolds sharper, punches hole 2 and throws. f208-215: Clank lifts its bars and gives a grudging nod through.
beats.concept: One-shot is a single pass, the lower bound. AlphaEvolve-style iterative refinement turns the failure into evaluator feedback and another attempt.
beats.camera: A slow push toward Evo, then a pan right with its throw.
beats.transition_out: Continuous camera move: the camera rises and orbits over the hub, following Evo's plane through the open gate and out over the GPU board.

beats.shot: B4 It runs, but it's off: high orbiting wide over the GPU board, craning down to an insert through Ref's magnifier.
beats.action: f216-243: the plane banks around the circuit past the spinning fan and over the heat-sink bleachers, trailing a halftone shadow across the gold traces. It swoops onto Evo's pad and lands a hair beside the inked reference outline (f244). f248-263: Ref waddles over, bends deep and raises the magnifier. The lens fills frame centre and shows the plane's nose poking past the outline by a sliver, with a coral ink tick on the gap. Ref's huge magnified eye squints. f264-279: whistle, and the coral-red flag snaps up with a flutter. Evo winces in the background with a sweat drop. f280-287: Ref flicks the plane back toward Evo.
beats.concept: The kernel runs on the GPU (the flight circuit over the board). Verification is against the PyTorch reference, and Pass@1 needs max abs error <= 0.01, so close is not correct.
beats.camera: Continues B3's orbit along the circuit, cranes down to the pad, then crash-pushes into the magnifier lens.
beats.transition_out: Match cut: the magnifier's round lens becomes the round dial of the brass stopwatch, same size and screen position.

beats.shot: B5 Right, but slower: from the stopwatch dial, pull back to a medium-wide of the pads and athletes.
beats.action: f288-299: the dial's gold and emerald hands tick back to zero. The pull-back reveals Evo clicking hole 3 with a fixed plane in hand, beside the Oracle. The Oracle throws with a lazy flick (no anticipation, pure swagger); Evo throws hard. f300-327: the two planes lap the circuit in the background with the gold a length ahead. The gold lands dead inside its outline first, with a ta-da pose from the Oracle; Evo's plane lands inside its outline a beat later. Ref green-flags both. f328-335: the stopwatch's gold hand stops first and the emerald hand a notch later. f336-359: the Oracle huffs on its handle-knuckles and buffs them on its chest. Ref hands Evo its plane back. Evo's eyes narrow and a sweat drop falls. Flash peeks out from under the towel.
beats.concept: Profile: being correct (Pass@1) isn't the whole story. Speed is compared with the hand-tuned oracle Triton kernel, and correct-but-slower means Perf@1 is below 1 (no number shown).
beats.camera: A pull-back from the dial, a slow push onto the stopwatch as the hands stop, then a pan to Evo.
beats.transition_out: Crash zoom (flash cut) straight into Evo's narrowing eyes.

beats.shot: B6 Rematch, WHOOSH: extreme close on Evo's eyes, a close on its hands, then a chase cam flying between the two planes.
beats.action: f360-383: Evo refolds with crisp creases, each one snapping on a beat, and adds an emerald stripe: a sleek dart. It punches hole 4, leaving one hole open. f384-395: Evo and the Oracle wind up in unison; Evo squashes almost into a disc for the anticipation. f396-401: release with a full stretch. f402-443: the chase cam rides between the gold plane and the emerald dart around the circuit. A hand-lettered "WHOOSH" is drawn along the path, speed lines streak, and the fan blades smear past. The gold leads, then the dart takes the inside line of the last bend and pulls ahead by a nose. f444-455: both dive toward the pads.
beats.concept: Iterative refinement: compile, verify and profile feedback have turned into a faster kernel, raced head-to-head against the oracle.
beats.camera: Crash-zoom out from the eyes to the hands, then a low chase cam (fov 40) that rolls with the banks.
beats.transition_out: Continuous camera move: the chase cam swings around ahead of the planes and cranes up to the stopwatch as they land.

beats.shot: B7 Perf@1 > 1: close on the stopwatch, craning down to a low wide under the scoring arch.
beats.action: f456-467: the emerald dart touches down dead inside its reference outline and Ref snaps the green flag. The stopwatch's emerald hand stops a clear notch before the gold hand, with an ink burst and no lettering; the gold plane lands a beat late. f468-483: extruded emerald block letters "Perf@1 > 1" drop from the arch beam on springy cords, squash on arrival, bounce with overshoot and settle by f484, with ink burst lines. f484-551 (hold of at least 1.5 s): Evo leaps with star eyes, clutching its card with one hole still open. The Oracle's jaw drops and its laurel slides over one eye. Flash yanks off his towel, jaw on the floor. Clank rattles its bars like applause.
beats.concept: Perf@1 = oracle latency / generated-kernel latency, and above 1 the generated kernel beats the hand-tuned oracle. It lands inside the outline (correct) and gets home first (faster).
beats.camera: Crane down from the dial to a low angle, with a 3% slow push and a slight orbit. An 8% punch and a shake on the letter slam, then a steady hold with the letters centred in rows ~330-600 and faces below.
beats.transition_out: Brush wipe: an emerald ink stroke sweeps left to right on Ref's whistle blast. Under full cover the letters retract into the beam and the pads are cleared.

beats.shot: B8 Next event: medium-wide of the hub, pulling back and rising to the home framing.
beats.action: f552-575: the wipe clears. Ref blows the whistle and the rolodex event deck ("164" on its base) whirrs through a flutter of operator cards before clacking to a stop. f576-611: Evo pops on a fresh punch card (five open holes) and takes a sheet. The Oracle picks up its golden plane and resumes buffing. Clank's bars sag back into a doze. f612-647: Flash springs off the bench with overshoot, flings the towel, grabs a fresh sheet and does cocky finger-guns (he hasn't learned). Everyone eases into their f0 poses.
beats.concept: The benchmark runs this event for every one of its 164 operators. Each event starts fresh, and the loop begins again.
beats.camera: A continuous pull back and rise that ends in the home push-in with exactly f0's pose and velocity.
beats.transition_out: Seamless loop: a continuous camera move into f0.

proposals.payoff:
The emerald dart, refined through four of Evo's five allowed attempts, lands inside the PyTorch reference outline (green flag, correct). The stopwatch's emerald hand stops a clear notch before the oracle's gold hand. Big extruded emerald block letters "Perf@1 > 1" (a smaller "Perf@1" beside a huge "> 1") slam down from the scoring arch under the "TritonGym" banner: centred, with the squash-bounce-overshoot landing, a punch and a shake, and a hold of at least 1.5 s. The reactions carry the meaning:
- Evo leaps with star eyes, one punch-card hole still open (up to 5 attempts).
- The golden Oracle's jaw drops and its laurel slips over one eye (the hand-tuned kernel has been beaten).
- Benched One-shot Flash yanks off his towel, jaw on the floor (the single pass stayed at the lower bound).

Only the Perf@1 > 1 fact and workflow behaviour are claimed. No model is named or ranked, and no other number is invented.
text_on_screen: TritonGym: hand-lettered on the cloth banner across the scoring arch (the only appearance of the name; clearest in B1 and the B7 payoff)
CLANG!: hand-lettered brush SFX at the compile gate (B2)
WHOOSH: hand-lettered SFX drawn along the flight path in the final race (B6)
Perf@1 > 1: the payoff, as extruded 3D emerald block letters (B7)
1: tiny inked number on Flash's bib (the single pass)
164: small painted number on the base of the rolodex event deck (optional; it states the operator count without a sentence)
proposals.loop_seam:
Frame 647 flows straight into frame 0.

- Camera: B8 ends on the same spline and velocity as B1's slow push-in and descent, so the move never stops or reverses.
- Payoff letters and landed planes: removed under B7's brush-wipe cover.
- Rolodex: its whirr in B8 is a full revolution through the deck (all 164 operators flicking by), so it clacks back onto the same matmul glyph shown from f0 (the film's loop is the benchmark's loop).
- Characters: in B8 each one lands in its f0 pose and in phase with its idle cycle. Flash holds a fresh sheet after his finger-guns, Evo has a fresh five-hole card and a sheet, the Oracle is mid-buff, Clank's doze-breathing and Ref's whistle twirl are periodic.
- Fan: turns at 72 frames per revolution, which divides 648.
- Ink boil and paper grain: seeded by frame mod 648.
- Paper stack: refilled to its f0 height under the wipe.

Check: the render hash of f648 equals f0.
proposals.why_clear:
It turns TritonGym's core claim into one sports gag a viewer can follow with the sound off.

- Workflows are athletes and the kernel is literally code on paper folded into a plane. The GPU is the arena the plane flies around.
- The benchmark's three standardised tools are three places and characters the plane must get past: the compile gate that clangs, the referee checking against the reference outline, and the stopwatch against the oracle. Every workflow meets the same tools and the same oracle, so the only difference shown is the workflow.
- Progress is spatial. Each attempt gets one station further: stopped at the gate, then landing off the outline, then correct but second, then first.
- The punch card makes "up to 5 attempts" countable and the bib makes "single pass" countable.
- The One-shot baseline is a running gag like the picture book's snail, so the contrast stays funny rather than lecturing.
- The payoff number is earned by what we just watched: correct (inside the outline) and faster than the hand-tuned oracle, which is exactly what Perf@1 > 1 means.
- Every beat has one read and maps to a real concept (compile, verify with tolerance, profile against the oracle, iterative refinement, single-pass lower bound, 164 operators).
- Nothing reads as a web page: no panels or charts, just a lit 3D gym with inked characters, a moving camera and story transitions.
proposals.risks:
- **Repetition of throws.** Each attempt fails at a different station with a different camera: a chase to the gate, an orbit and magnifier insert, a dial match cut, then a race chase. Attempts 3 and 4 are side-by-side with the Oracle, so the escalation stays visible.
- **Planes too small at 400 px.** Build them about Evo's body width with 6-9 px ink. Frame the landings and the magnifier insert large, and test the card crop early.
- **The landing-on-the-outline metaphor for correctness** may be read loosely. The magnifier plus the coral gap tick sells "a tiny difference still fails (<= 0.01)". Keep the outline a thick, clear plane silhouette on each pad.
- **Accuracy framing.** It is one event of one benchmark. Never show a model name or a ranking, and do not imply One-shot always fails or iteration always beats the oracle: one sprinter, one event, and the bib and card only show attempt counts. The Oracle is the hand-tuned kernel, not a rival model. Evo's name is internal only; no "AlphaEvolve" text appears on screen.
- **Palette creep.** The Oracle and stopwatch brass is a third hue. Keep it a desaturated ochre warm neutral like the comic reference, with emerald dominant and coral the only pop.
- **Stopwatch echoes Qubrio's pocket-watch character Tick.** Keep it a pillar-mounted prop with two hands, never a character.
- **Busy beats.** In B3 (Flash benched plus Evo's feedback) and B8 (reset), stagger the actions by at least 8 frames with one leading action each. Cut Clank's applause or the rolodex flutter if the review says they compete.
- **Flight path hidden.** The circuit behind the arch must stay readable: keep it wide and high, and avoid passing behind pillars at key moments.
- **Text budget.** The bib "1" and deck "164" are tiny labels; drop "164" if the text feels heavy.
- **CPU render cost.** Around 40 pins, 7 bars, 2 fans and 3 planes are modest. Use shaders (not particles) for speed lines and confetti-free bursts.
- **Seamless loop.** Needs the rolodex full revolution, periodic idles and the paper-stack refill under the wipe to be exact; verify with an f0 vs f648 render hash.

proposals.title: The Loop Circuit
proposals.logline: An LLM athlete with a speech-bubble head builds a little racing kernel out of its own code tokens. It then takes the kernel round the TritonGym circuit: the compile gate slams on a crooked token, the referee's scale checks it against the PyTorch torch, and it loses a stopwatch race to the hand-tuned oracle champion because it has square wheels. One refinement later it goes round again and wins the rematch by a nose: Perf@1 > 1. Then the athlete dashes back to the bench for the next operator, and the film loops.

cast.name: Tok (the LLM athlete)
cast.concept: The LLM under test, acting as the agent in the loop. It writes the kernel, reads the tools' feedback and refines. A speech-bubble head says 'language model', and its code comes out as tokens.
cast.design: Head: a big cream speech bubble, made from a squashed sphere (1.3 x 1 x 0.85) plus a short cone for the bubble's tail at the lower back. It has a thick ink outline. Around the head is an emerald sweatband (a torus) whose two knot tails are flattened capsules that flap on every move. Face: two black ink dot eyes that go to slits when it concentrates. A mouth appears only on takes: an 'O' when it pops tokens, a grin, star eyes at the payoff. Body: a small capsule torso in an emerald singlet with one cream stripe. Arms are noodle tubes with white mitten spheres; legs are thin tubes ending in big coral sneakers (squashed spheres on white disc soles). The head is about half its height. Acting: skid-stop squash, knuckle-crack anticipation (the head inflates taller), an idea take where the head stretches up, a sprinter crouch, and a star-eyed leap.
cast.silhouette: A big round balloon with one spike on a tiny body, with headband tails flicking off the back: a lollipop on legs. Nothing else in the film is round on top and tall.

cast.name: Kern (the generated Triton kernel)
cast.concept: The kernel the LLM writes. It is built from Tok's tokens, so it is literally code. While it is uncompiled source it has a patchwork cream-token skin; it turns solid emerald once it passes the compile gate. It is a wind-up racer, because profiling measures how fast it runs. Its square wheels stand for a correct but slow implementation.
cast.design: A stubby horizontal capsule (soapbox-racer bullet) with a flattened underside, knee-high to Tok. As source code its shell is a mosaic of about 11 cream token tiles (small rounded cubes stamped with ink squiggles such as a brace, an equals sign and a star, never words). It floods to solid matte emerald #059669 with faint ink seams after compiling. On its back is a wind-up key (a flattened torus loop on a short cylinder) that spins while it runs. It has two headlight eyes on the front: white discs with black dot pupils, plus lids for emotion (spiral when dizzy, droopy when beaten, a grin when it wins). First version: four coral CUBE wheels and one crooked token sticking up like a cowlick (the compile bug). After refinement: four round coral disc wheels with cream hubs and a pointed cone nose token.
cast.silhouette: A short, low bullet with a key loop on top. The first version is jagged (square wheels plus cowlick); the refined one is sleek (round wheels plus pointed nose). Its low, horizontal read is the opposite of Tok's tall one.

cast.name: Oro (the oracle champion)
cast.concept: The hand-tuned oracle Triton kernel, the speed bar that Perf@1 divides by. It is the same species as Kern (a racer), so the race is a fair kernel-vs-kernel comparison on the same track. The champion look means 'the expert's gold standard', and the visible tuning knobs mean 'hand-tuned'.
cast.design: A long, low capsule body in the coral pop colour (complementary to emerald) with a pointed cone nose, a small flattened-cone tail fin, and round spoked wheels (cylinders with thin ink spokes). A gold laurel wreath (a torus ring of small leaf ellipsoids) sits around its wind-up key. Two neat rows of tiny brass tuning knobs (short cylinders) run along its flank. Headlight eyes are heavy-lidded and smug. Acting: a slow side-eye at the start, a double-take and sweat drop in the rematch, a jaw drop at the finish, then a sporting nod.
cast.silhouette: A long coral dart with a fin at the back and a gold ring on top, about 1.6 times Kern's length. It reads as a horizontal arrow next to Kern's stubby bullet.

cast.name: Ref (the verify referee / balance scale)
cast.concept: The verify tool: correctness is checked against the PyTorch reference, and Pass@1 requires max absolute error <= 0.01. Ref is a balance scale. The PyTorch reference sits on one pan as a 'torch': a stout cream torch with a coral flame, a pun and not a logo. The dial on Ref's chest has a hair-thin green tolerance notch, and the needle must settle inside it.
cast.design: The body is a tall cylinder column painted in black-and-white vertical referee stripes. The head is a sphere with slit eyes and a short cylinder whistle at the mouth. The arms are the balance beam, one long horizontal cylinder pivoting at the shoulders with ball ends. Two shallow dish pans hang from them on thin cylinder rods. On the chest is a round cream dial with one black needle and a very thin emerald notch at the top. A green flag (a small plane on a stick) is tucked at its side. The right pan holds the reference torch: a cream cylinder handle, a cup, and a coral teardrop-cone flame that flickers slowly.
cast.silhouette: A tall striped pole topped by a wide horizontal beam with two hanging dishes, a big T or Y shape. It is the only tall, thin, symmetric shape in the film.

cast.name: The Compile Gate
cast.concept: The compile tool. Malformed code does not fit: the crooked token clips a height-gauge bar and the portcullis slams shut. That error sends Kern straight back to Tok as feedback. Code that fits passes through and comes out compiled (paper tokens become solid emerald).
cast.design: A squat riveted steel arch: two chunky box piers joined by a half-torus top, cel-shaded slate grey with ink rivet dots. A striped yellow-and-ink height-gauge bar hangs from chains just inside the mouth. Behind it is a portcullis made of about 8 vertical cylinder bars with pointed tips. Two rivets above the arch act as 'eyes' that narrow just before the slam. It is a prop with a flicker of personality, not a talking character.
cast.silhouette: A low, heavy doorway with a toothy portcullis: it reads as a mouth that bites.

cast.name: The Stopwatch Tower
cast.concept: The profile tool: it times latency. It is a split-time stopwatch with an emerald hand for Kern and a coral hand for Oro. Which hand stops first shows who ran faster, with no chart and no numbers. The emerald hand stopping short of the coral hand is exactly Perf@1 > 1 (oracle latency / generated latency).
cast.design: A giant brass-and-cream stopwatch face (a flattened cylinder disc with an ink tick ring) on a tall post at the finish line. It has a crown button (a small cylinder plus a torus ring) that plunges with a CLICK pose, and two thick hands, one emerald and one coral. No face or limbs. It stands left of centre in the finish-line shots so it never sits under the LIVE pill.
cast.silhouette: A big round disc on a pole with a knob on top, a lollipop sign. It is kept smaller and further back than Tok so the two round-top shapes never compete.

proposals.world:
THE TRITONGYM ARENA is one continuous three.js set: a round indoor gym whose running track is a giant emerald GPU circuit board. The track surface is matte emerald PCB. The lane lines are cream-gold copper traces with solder-pad dots, and they pulse with a flat inked ripple (never bloom) when a kernel runs. The infield is a big slate-grey GPU die with a heat-spreader lid and a slowly turning cooling-fan grille. The camera rides a circular dolly around this die, looking out at the stations, and its yaw makes exactly one 360-degree turn per loop, so the film is literally a lap.

Stations sit around the oval in loop order (camera yaw):
- 0 degrees: the WORKBENCH (write/refine), a chunky wooden bench just past the start/finish line, with a hand-lettered board on its front apron reading 'TritonGym'.
- 80 degrees: the COMPILE GATE.
- 160 degrees: REF'S SCALE (verify).
- 220 to 320 degrees: the SPRINT STRAIGHT (profile), from a painted start line down to the finish line and the Stopwatch Tower.
- 360 degrees: back at the bench.

Depth layers behind every station: the track, the station, a low padded wall, three tiers of simple empty cream-ochre bleachers, pennant bunting (triangles) strung across, tall windows of warm painted paper sky, and 4 to 5 hanging gym lamps with cone shades. The lamps are real spot lights feeding the toon ramp and pool warm light on the track, with halftone falling off into the shadows. There are no crowds; a few gym props (a coiled rope, a medicine ball) are kept sparse.

Palette: emerald #059669 dominant (track, Kern, Tok's singlet), coral as the single complementary pop (Oro, sneakers, wheels, torch flame, CLANG!), ink black, and warm cream paper, with small ochre accents (laurel, lamp light). The look follows reference/style-comic: cel ramp, boiling ink at style-comic weight, halftone, off-register print and paper grain.

Card safety: every key action and face sits in master rows 180 to 835. Nothing important goes top-right (x > 1590, y 130 to 300); the Stopwatch Tower and the payoff letters stay centre or left of centre.

beats.shot: B1 WRITE: medium, low three-quarter on the workbench; the 'TritonGym' board on its apron sits low in frame
beats.action: f0-8: the whip from B8 lands. Tok skids in from frame-left and stops at the bench with a squash and a dust puff. f8-22: Tok cracks its mitten knuckles, headband tails flick, and it inhales; its bubble head swells taller (anticipation). f22-54: Tok 'says' the code. Its mouth pops open every 3rd frame, and about 11 cream token tiles (ink squiggles, never words) hop out in arcs and click together on the bench into a stubby capsule body. Four SQUARE token blocks plonk underneath as wheels. The last token lands crooked, sticking up like a cowlick, and Tok doesn't notice. f54-68: two headlight eyes blink open and Kern is alive. It wiggles, and Tok winds the key on its back: three cranks, with Kern squashing on each. f68-83: Kern hops down to the track (squash, overshoot) and Tok flings an arm toward the gate in a 'go!' pose.
beats.concept: An LLM writes a Triton kernel token by token, so the kernel is literally made of the model's output. The crooked token plants a compile bug.
beats.camera: Lands out of the whip with the smear fading over f0-8. Then a slow push from medium to medium-close with a small crane-down following the token arcs, and a 4-degree dutch that settles level. It pans right with Kern as it hops off.
beats.transition_out: Whip pan right (motion smear plus speed lines) following Kern round the track to the Compile Gate.

beats.shot: B2 COMPILE: low three-quarter angle beside Tok, facing the riveted steel gate arch with its striped height-gauge bar and raised portcullis
beats.action: f84-100: Kern trundles up on square wheels, its body bobbing on every flat face, with Tok jogging behind. f100-104: the crooked token clips the gauge bar, the bar swings, and the gate's rivet 'eyes' narrow. f104-110: the portcullis SLAMS down with 'CLANG!' in jagged coral letters, a 2-frame black-and-white impact frame and a shake. Kern ricochets back spinning and lands in Tok's arms; both squash and Kern's eyes spiral. f110-132: Tok spots the crooked token, frowns, and presses it flat with a thumb. Kern winces, then brightens. f132-155: the portcullis grinds up and Kern rolls under the gauge bar without touching it. As it crosses the gate line, its cream token patchwork floods solid emerald in one ripple.
beats.concept: COMPILE (one of the standardised tools): badly formed code is rejected and the error feeds straight back to the LLM. The fixed code compiles into a runnable kernel (paper source becomes solid emerald).
beats.camera: Low and close to the floor. A 6% punch-in plus shake on the CLANG, with a 2-frame impact frame. Then a continuous dolly behind Kern that follows it under the arch.
beats.transition_out: Continuous camera move through the gate arch: the dark arch frame sweeps across the whole screen like a wipe and opens on Ref.

beats.shot: B3 VERIFY: medium-wide, eye level on Ref's full T-shape. The PyTorch torch (cream, coral flame) sits on the right pan and the left pan is empty.
beats.action: f156-166: Kern rolls up a tiny ramp onto the left pan. f166-194: the beam lurches: Kern's side dips, overshoots up and wobbles. The needle on Ref's chest dial swings past the hair-thin green notch twice while Ref's slit eyes track it and Tok bites its mitten in the background. Then the needle settles dead inside the notch. f194-215: Ref blows its whistle (three ink puff lines) and snaps up a green flag. Kern sags with relief and Tok pumps a fist.
beats.concept: VERIFY / Pass@1: the kernel is checked against the PyTorch reference. The hair-thin notch is the tolerance (max absolute error <= 0.01), and the green flag means correct.
beats.camera: Opens out of the arch into the wide. A slow push-in toward the dial and Kern's face as the needle hunts (fov narrowing slightly), then a tilt up with the flag.
beats.transition_out: Brush wipe: Ref's green flag swishes across the lens, and the cut to the sprint start line hides under full cover.

beats.shot: B4 PROFILE RACE 1: low, tense two-shot on the painted start line. Kern (solid emerald, still on square wheels) sits beside Oro (long coral racer, gold laurel), with the Stopwatch Tower small at the far end of the straight.
beats.action: f216-236: Oro revs, and its knobs and laurel shiver. It gives Kern a slow, smug side-eye and Kern gulps. f236-240: the stopwatch crown clicks down and both launch. f240-280: Oro rockets off, stretched with speed lines, and is gone. Kern lurches forward: each flat face slams down and bounces its body, and one hand-lettered 'THUNK' bounces beside a wheel. Tok runs along the inner lane cheering, then covers its eyes. f280-311: at the finish line Oro is already parked, buffing its laurel, and the coral hand on the Stopwatch Tower stopped long ago. Kern clunks across puffing steam from its key, sweat drops flying, and the emerald hand finally stops far past the coral one.
beats.concept: PROFILE: latency is measured against the hand-tuned oracle Triton kernel. The kernel is correct but slower, so Perf@1 < 1. Square wheels mean it works but it is slow.
beats.camera: A slow push toward the two faces at the start. On the CLICK, a fast low lateral tracking dolly at Oro's speed that loses it, then decelerates to hold the lumbering Kern (the gag), then pans ahead onto the finish line and the stopwatch.
beats.transition_out: Crash zoom (continuous push) into Kern's square wheel, landing on B5's close-up.

beats.shot: B5 REFINE: medium-close at the finish line on Kern's square wheel, with Tok kneeling beside it
beats.action: f312-324: Tok stares at the square wheel, then its eyes pop and its bubble head stretches up: the idea take. f324-350: Tok pops out five fresh tokens. The square wheels pop off, and one flops end over end away because it can't roll (the gag). Four ROUND wheels snap on with overshoot, and a pointed nose token clicks onto Kern's front. The new pieces are cream: fresh, uncompiled code. f350-371: Kern revs, its new wheels spin in place throwing ink smoke rings, and it grins. Tok drops into a sprinter's crouch beside it.
beats.concept: ITERATIVE REFINEMENT: using the profiler's feedback, the LLM edits specific parts of its kernel rather than starting over.
beats.camera: Opens on the crash-zoomed wheel, then a slow 60-degree orbit round Kern during the wheel swap so the 3D parts read. It ends low and wide, ready to launch.
beats.transition_out: Whip pan with smear as Kern and Tok launch into lap 2.

beats.shot: B6 AGAIN: a fast travelling shot round the circuit with Kern and Tok, the stations flashing past
beats.action: f372-388: Kern zips under the Compile Gate's raised portcullis, clearing the gauge bar, and its cream new parts flash emerald (compiled again). f388-406: Kern hops onto Ref's pan. One quick dip, the needle lands in the notch at once, the green flag snaps up, and Ref gives a short toot. Kern hops off. f406-419: Kern skids onto the start line beside a waiting Oro, with Tok alongside, catching its breath.
beats.concept: The agent loop repeats: every refinement goes through the same standardised tools again (compile, then verify, then profile).
beats.camera: One continuous fast dolly-crane arc round the GPU die infield, with the stations whipping past, speed lines, and a slight speed ramp. It decelerates into the exact start-line composition of B4.
beats.transition_out: Continuous camera move that settles into B4's start-line framing exactly, a deliberate 'rematch' rhyme.

beats.shot: B7 PROFILE RACE 2: the same low start-line two-shot as B4, then a side tracking shot down the straight
beats.action: f420-432: Oro starts the same smug side-eye, then does a double-take at Kern's round wheels and nose, and a sweat drop pops. f432-436: the crown CLICKs and both launch. f436-488: they run neck and neck. Kern's key spins in a blur, Oro squeezes its eyes shut and strains, and Tok sprints on the inner lane with its legs a cartoon wheel. They trade the lead once. f488-503: at the line Kern stretches its pointed nose forward, and the photo-finish camera flashes.
beats.concept: PROFILE again: the refined kernel's latency is now below the oracle's. It is a narrow, honest win on this one operator.
beats.camera: Opens identical to B4's framing, then a fast low side-tracking dolly at racer speed with a dutch that increases toward the line, and a small push-in at the finish.
beats.transition_out: Flash cut: the photo-finish flash (one white frame, then a 2-frame black-and-white impact freeze).

beats.shot: B8 PAYOFF: low hero angle facing the finish line. The Stopwatch Tower is behind, left of centre, and the payoff letters are centre-frame above the racers.
beats.action: f504-510: the black-and-white freeze shows Kern's nose a hair over the line ahead of Oro's, then colour returns. f510-520: on the Stopwatch Tower, the emerald hand has stopped just short of the coral hand, because Kern's run took less time. f520-534: 'Perf@1 > 1' in extruded 3D block letters (emerald faces, coral sides) drops from above and slams onto the finish line in the centre of frame, with squash, overshoot, a dust ring and a shake. 'Perf@1' is smaller on top and a huge '> 1' below. f534-580: Tok leaps with star eyes to the left, never in front of the letters. Kern bounces and grins. Oro's jaw drops and a sweat drop pops, then it gives a sporting nod and tips its laurel. Tok and Kern bump, mitten to nose. f580-599: Tok's head snaps toward the bench off-frame right (the next operator is waiting), its legs wind up, and it zips off.
beats.concept: PAYOFF: Perf@1 = oracle latency / generated latency. Perf@1 > 1 means the LLM-written kernel beat the hand-tuned oracle. Tok then heads straight back to the bench, because the benchmark is many operators and the loop continues.
beats.camera: A slow push-in with a 15-degree orbit so the 3D letters parallax against the stopwatch and bleachers, with a shake on the slam. It ends with a whip pan right after Tok.
beats.transition_out: Whip pan right (smear) following Tok to the workbench. The whip continues across the loop seam into frame 0.

proposals.payoff: In the rematch, the refined emerald kernel noses over the finish line a hair ahead of the coral oracle champion. The photo-finish flash freezes it, and the split stopwatch shows the emerald hand stopped short of the coral one. Then 'Perf@1 > 1' slams down as extruded 3D block letters in the centre of frame: the LLM-written Triton kernel beat the hand-tuned oracle. The earlier beats make the win meaningful: CLANG at the compile gate, the needle settling in the hair-thin tolerance notch on the verify scale (Pass@1 vs the PyTorch reference), and the square-wheel loss. The narrow margin keeps it honest, since Perf@1 > 1 only means 'faster than the oracle'. Tok's dash back to the bench says this was one operator on a benchmark, not 'winning TritonGym'.
text_on_screen: TritonGym: hand-lettered in emerald brush capitals on the workbench's front board (B1, the only appearance of the name)
CLANG!: jagged coral hand-lettered SFX at the compile gate slam (B2)
THUNK: one small ink-lettered SFX bouncing beside a square wheel in the lost race (B4)
Perf@1 > 1: extruded 3D block letters slammed onto the finish line, with 'Perf@1' smaller on top and a huge '> 1' below (B8 payoff)
proposals.loop_seam:
The camera yaw makes exactly one 360-degree turn round the GPU-die infield per loop, so the last move (B8, f580-599) is the whip pan from the finish line to the workbench. That whip runs straight through the seam: yaw, angular velocity, smear amount and Tok's run velocity at f599 equal the values extrapolated into f0. At f0-8 the camera decelerates onto the bench as Tok skids in with a squash.

All state resets happen off-camera, behind the whip: the winning Kern, Oro and the 'Perf@1 > 1' letters stay at the finish line and are removed; Oro reappears waiting at the sprint start; the stopwatch hands reset.

Frame 0 never shows the finish line; the bench shot frames only the bench, Tok and the 'TritonGym' board. The seam is motivated in the story: Tok rushes to the next operator, and a new kernel is written. Check that f600 would hash-equal f0. The card loop can be rotated to start at the poster frame at no cost.
proposals.poster_moment: About f545 (22.7 s), during B8's hold. 'Perf@1 > 1' in emerald-and-coral 3D block letters has just landed in the centre of frame on the finish line, with dust settling. Below it, Kern (solid emerald, round wheels, pointed nose) grins with its nose over the line at left of centre. Oro (coral, laurel) is at right with its jaw dropped. Tok hangs mid-leap with star eyes at left, clear of the letters. The Stopwatch Tower behind, left of centre, shows the emerald hand stopped short of the coral hand. Everything sits inside rows 180-835, with nothing in the top-right LIVE-pill zone.
proposals.why_clear:
Each of TritonGym's three standardised tools is a physical station that does exactly its job, in the order an agent loop uses them:
- the compile gate rejects the crooked token (badly formed code) and passes the fixed one, which comes out solid, i.e. compiled;
- the referee's scale weighs the kernel against the PyTorch torch, and the needle must land in a hair-thin notch (Pass@1, max absolute error <= 0.01);
- the split stopwatch races it against the hand-tuned oracle champion (Perf@1).

The kernel is a clear physical thing, a little wind-up racer made of the LLM's own tokens. Refinement is a readable edit: square wheels swapped for round ones. The circuit is literally a loop: the camera circles the track once per film, lap 2 visibly re-runs compile and verify, and Tok's dash to the next operator is the loop seam.

The conflict is kept small and funny: a CLANG, then 'correct but slow' shown as square wheels going THUNK. The payoff is a single headline fact, the kernel beating the oracle by a nose, stated once as 'Perf@1 > 1'.

Every beat has one read and a reaction shot (Tok's takes, Kern's eyes, Oro's side-eye turning into a double-take), and every transition is a real camera move or a story object: whip, arch wipe, flag wipe, crash zoom, match framing, photo-finish flash.

There are no panels, charts, labels or sentences. The only text is the name once, two SFX and the payoff.
proposals.risks:
1. The metaphor needs the viewer to accept 'cart = kernel'. B1 must clearly show the tokens coming from Tok and building Kern, and B2's cream-to-emerald compile ripple must read. Test B1 at card size; if the tokens are too small, use fewer and bigger ones (8 to 9).
2. The balance scale simplifies elementwise max-abs-error to one needle. The domain lens may note that weight is a scalar. Mitigations: keep the notch hair-thin, keep the torch clearly the reference, and optionally have Kern drop a small emerald output block onto the pan instead of weighing itself.
3. Why round wheels plus a nose beat the oracle is left metaphorical, because no specific optimisation is claimed. Keep the win a nose-ahead photo finish; never show a blowout or a ratio number.
4. Tok's speech-bubble head could read as a chat-UI icon. It must be a fully lit 3D cel/halftone object with a headband, body and acting, never flat. Token-popping must read as 'speaking' (upward hops on beat), not spitting.
5. B1, B2 and B6 are dense. Keep one action on screen at a time, and pose to the beat grid. If B6 is too fast at 48 frames, borrow 12 from B4's lead-in.
6. The 3D glyphs '@' and '>' must stay legible at 400 px. Stack the letters, make '> 1' the largest, face the camera within 20 degrees, and test the 2.1 to 2.64:1 crops.
7. Continuity cheats hidden behind whips and the flag wipe: Oro returns to the start line unseen, the previous Kern is removed at the seam, and the stopwatch resets. Frame 0 and B4's start must never show the finish line with leftover payoff objects.
8. Tok and the Stopwatch Tower are both round-on-top. Keep the tower behind and smaller, and left of centre, so it never sits under the top-right LIVE pill.
9. Render cost is fine: about 30 small token and wheel meshes, about 8 portcullis bars, a few carts, and extruded text for about 9 glyphs. Speed lines, SFX and faces are 2D ink tracked to 3D. Whips use npr.setSmear on a single render, never cross-dissolves.
10. Oro is coral while the brief says emerald dominates. Coral is the one complementary pop, and the track, Kern and Tok keep emerald dominant in every frame.

proposals.title: Circuit Training
proposals.logline: The gym is a GPU and the workout is a loop. A comic speech balloon (the LLM) writes a paper-scroll runner (a Triton kernel) and sends it round a circuit of three stations that are the same for everyone: the compile gate, a weigh-in against the PyTorch torch, and a stopwatch race against a brass, hand-wound champion (the oracle). After each failure the runner comes back to the balloon to be patched. It is stamped Pass@1, then beats the champion (Perf@1 > 1), and the balloon picks the next sheet off a stack of 164.

cast.name: Chatter
cast.concept: The LLM, a language model shown as a comic speech balloon. It writes the Triton kernel, reads the tools' feedback and refines the kernel. It is the agent at the centre of the workflow.
cast.design: A cream-white speech balloon: a superellipse Shape extruded 0.35 deep with a bevel, about 1.3 wide by 1.0 tall. A curved pointed tail extruded from the bottom-left edge is its only foot; it hops on it like a pogo, squashing the balloon on each landing. Two capsule arms end in sphere mittens. It carries a big coral pencil (hex prism, cone tip, emerald ferrule, eraser cylinder) and wears a coral whistle (cylinder plus torus) on an emerald cord. The face is two ink dot eyes set high on the balloon. Three emerald squiggle 'word' lines sit under the eyes and ripple only while it writes; they are the same squiggles that land on the page. The mouth appears only on takes (an 'o' gulp, a whistle pucker). Heavy ink hull and halftone so it reads as a comic balloon, not a chat UI. It has no '...' typing dots.
cast.silhouette: A wide, rounded slab balanced on one curved spike. It reads as 'speech balloon = language' at 400 px, and no other cast member looks like it.

cast.name: Kern
cast.concept: The Triton GPU kernel the LLM writes: the code itself, which is the thing that gets compiled, verified and timed. Each coral patch is one refinement (a diff-style edit).
cast.design: A rolled paper scroll standing upright. It is an open cylinder made by extruding a spiral cross-section, so the curled seam shows, and its top lip curls back like a cowlick. The paper is cream, printed with emerald code squiggles and a tiny emerald trident crest (Triton). It has thin capsule stick arms and legs with coral sneaker ellipsoids, and dot eyes printed on the paper; a mouth only on takes. States: born (a flat sheet rolled up by a bend deformer); crumpled (a swap to a noise-displaced icosphere in the same paper material, hidden under a 2-frame impact frame); patched (coral square decals with stitch ticks); stamped (an emerald 'Pass@1' ink decal); sleek (radius -20 %, height +10 %, a coral headband torus with two ribbon tails).
cast.silhouette: A narrow tall tube on stick legs with a paper curl on top. It is the only vertical, straight-sided figure in the cast.

cast.name: The Oracle
cast.concept: The hand-tuned oracle Triton kernel that the profiler times against: the speed to beat. Perf@1 = oracle latency / kernel latency.
cast.design: A brass wind-up champion. The body is a tapered brass cylinder (frustum) with two riveted bands, faint engraved code squiggles and the same trident crest in gold (it is a Triton kernel too, only handmade). The head is a sphere with slit eyes, smug by default, under a gold laurel ring (a torus with small extruded leaves). A large flat butterfly wind-up key sticks out of its back, and it turns the key itself: hand-wound = hand-tuned. It has piston legs (cylinders) with disc feet and stands about 1.4 times Kern's height. Acting: a self-winding click-click, calf stretches, a smug once-over; eyes pop and the key spins frantically when it is overtaken; a sporting tip of the laurel and a handshake.
cast.silhouette: A tall tapered figure with the butterfly key sticking out of its back. It is the tallest cast member and has the most mechanical profile.

cast.name: Torchy
cast.concept: The PyTorch reference implementation that correctness is checked against (max absolute error <= 0.01).
cast.design: A squat torch. It has a dark-emerald tapered-cone handle and a cream cup with ink dot eyes. On top is a flat, cel-shaded coral-orange flame made of three stacked teardrops, with an ink outline and a vertex wobble; there is no bloom or glow. It has stubby capsule arms and carries an emerald rubber stamp (cylinder knob plus block). Acting: arms crossed, a squint at the needle, a nod, the stamp THUNK; the flame leans as the beam tilts and flares when it is pleased.
cast.silhouette: A short cone topped by a pointed, flickering flame. ML viewers read 'torch = PyTorch'.

proposals.world: One continuous three.js set: a gym built on a GPU, in which the running track is literally a circuit ('circuit training' on a circuit board). The floor is an emerald printed-circuit board (#059669, with darker halftone in the shadows) with solder-dot pads. The two-lane running oval is laid in inked gold traces around a central GPU die: a big black square block with a gold heat-spreader lid, no brand. The back straight runs across the die's edge, so the races are run on the GPU. Behind is a gym wall of graphite heat-sink fins (tall thin slabs, halftoned), with one large cooling fan shroud turning slowly like a gym clock. Inked cone lamps hang from above, and there are a few low black chip-blocks for benches (legless, sitting on pads). The stations follow the order the tools run, round the oval: (1) the coach's bench at front-left, with a small chalk tally board and a tall stack of blank sheets banded cream / crinkly coral / ink-glyph edged, under a hand-painted 'TritonGym' sign; (2) the Compile Gate at front-right, an emerald turnstile arch with three chunky bars and a round lamp that goes amber then coral or emerald; (3) the Weigh-in on the right curve, a big brass balance with a dial whose needle has a hairline emerald tolerance notch; (4) the sprint straight on the far side, with start blocks, ending at the Stopwatch Arch, a giant stopwatch ring standing on edge with a crown button on top and two hands (gold for the oracle, coral for Kern); (5) the left curve back to the bench. The camera travels this loop, so the film's loop is the agent loop. Look: the style-comic NPR (cel ramp, boiling ink hull plus screen edges, halftone, slight off-register, paper grain), warm cream paper light, emerald dominant, coral (#E8553A) as the single pop colour, ink black. All sci-fi elements (traces, fan, die) are inked and flat-lit: no neon, no HUD. The far areas are painted cards so there is depth, never a flat colour backdrop.

beats.shot: WRITE: medium 3/4 on Chatter at its bench, a blank sheet on the desk, the tall sheet stack cropped at frame-left.
beats.action: f0: Chatter, pencil raised, leans back in anticipation with narrowed eyes. f6-40: a scribble frenzy. The pencil zigzags and rows of emerald code squiggles ink onto the sheet (2D ink tracked to the sheet); the same squiggles ripple across Chatter's balloon; its body jiggles on each stroke and the spike foot taps. f41-56: a final dot flourish, and the sheet curls itself up into a scroll (bend deformer) and springs upright on stick legs. Kern is born: it lands in a squash, stretches, and two dot eyes blink open with the trident crest showing. f57-71: Kern glances up at Chatter, then down the track. Chatter blows the coral whistle (a small ink puff), and Kern crouches and bolts to the right.
beats.concept: An LLM writes a Triton GPU kernel. The language model (the speech balloon) turns text into code, and that code is what will run.
beats.camera: A slow push from medium to medium-close over f0-40 (fov 32 -> 29) with a 2 degree dutch. On the bolt, a quick pan right that turns into a truck right at Kern's speed.
beats.transition_out: Continuous camera move: the truck right carries straight into beat 2 alongside Kern.

beats.shot: COMPILE -> CLANG!: a knee-height tracking shot to the Compile Gate.
beats.action: f72-95: Kern sprints (legs on twos) toward the emerald turnstile gate. f96-104: it skids up and the round lamp blinks amber while it reads the code, then turns coral. f105-110: the bars SLAM shut. A 2-frame black-and-white impact frame, a 6 % punch-in and a shake; hand-lettered 'CLANG!' bursts left of the gate. Kern faceplants into the bars and crumples into a paper ball (the mesh swap is hidden under the impact frame). A small error slip with a coral X squiggle spits out of the gate's slot. f111-130: a held beat. The ball wobbles, and one dizzy spiral eye peeks out of a fold. f131-143: one bar swings like a bat and whacks the ball and the slip back over camera-left.
beats.concept: The compile tool: the kernel must compile. The first, one-shot attempt fails, and one-shot is the lower bound.
beats.camera: A tracking dolly, then a crash zoom on the slam (fov 34 -> 24) with a shake. Hold, then a whip left that follows the ball.
beats.transition_out: Whip pan with smear streaks, following the flying paper ball back to the coach's bench.

beats.shot: FEEDBACK -> PATCH: a medium two-shot at the bench, 3/4 low.
beats.action: f144-152: Chatter catches the ball, is knocked back a hop and squashes. The error slip flutters onto its face; it peels it off and reads it, squinting. f153-180: it uncrumples the ball and Kern pops back into a cylinder with spiral dizzy eyes. Chatter licks the pencil, scribbles one decisive fix on exactly the spot the slip marked, and slaps a coral stitched patch over it (the diff). A second chalk tally ticks onto the board behind. f181-200: Kern shakes itself like a wet dog (paper flutter), its eyes clear and narrow, and it pats the patch. f201-215: the whistle, and Kern bolts right again.
beats.concept: The agent loop: feedback from the tools goes back to the LLM, which edits the kernel and tries again (iterative refinement with diff-style edits).
beats.camera: The whip lands on the two-shot, with a 5 % push on the patch slap, then pans right with the bolt.
beats.transition_out: Continuous camera move with no cut. The camera rides with Kern back through the gate, whose lamp flips emerald and whose bars swing open with a friendly bounce (compile passes), and carries on to the scale.

beats.shot: VERIFY -> Pass@1: the weigh-in on the right curve, a low 3/4 with the balance filling the centre.
beats.action: f216-230: Torchy stands on the right pan, arms crossed, flame flickering; Kern leaps onto the left pan. f231-262: the beam slams down on Kern's side, overshoots up and wobbles in a damped oscillation. Kern windmills its arms, Torchy's flame leans with each tilt, and the dial needle swings. f263-275: the beam settles dead level and the needle drops into the hairline emerald notch (the <= 0.01 tolerance). Both freeze, and Torchy leans in and squints. f276-299: Torchy nods, raises its emerald rubber stamp and THUNKs it onto Kern (stamp squash, Kern squash). An ink print reading 'Pass@1' appears on Kern's paper. Kern blushes and grins, and Torchy's flame flares happily.
beats.concept: The verify tool: the kernel's output must match the PyTorch reference within a maximum absolute error of 0.01. That is Pass@1.
beats.camera: On the settle, a quick 12-frame push to the needle and notch, then a pull back out for the stamp.
beats.transition_out: Continuous camera move: Kern springs off the pan, and the camera crane-arcs up and over with its leap, landing at the start line of the sprint straight.

beats.shot: PROFILE RACE, lost by a nose: the start line on the back straight across the GPU die.
beats.action: f300-318: Kern lands beside the Oracle, which is winding its own key (click-click), stretching and looking Kern up and down with smug slit eyes. Kern gulps and a sweat drop pops. f319-324: the Stopwatch Arch's crown button presses down: GO. f325-360: a side-by-side race along the gold trace lanes. The Oracle pistons smoothly while Kern pumps frantically, its paper flapping. They are neck and neck, then the Oracle edges ahead. f361-370: the Oracle crosses first under the arch, by a nose; the gold hand stops, and the coral hand stops a tick later. f371-383: Kern skids through and droops, body sagging and eyes drooping, while the Oracle buffs its laurel.
beats.concept: The profile tool: the kernel's latency is timed against the hand-tuned oracle Triton kernel, on the GPU. It is correct but slower, so Perf@1 is below 1.
beats.camera: A low 3/4 at the start line, then a side dolly at race speed with speed lines (fov 34), and a small push as they cross.
beats.transition_out: Whip pan with smear back along the loop to the coach. Every failure returns to the LLM; this is the second time, so the grammar is learned.

beats.shot: PATCH AGAIN + RE-RUN: close on Chatter's hands, then a streak round the circuit.
beats.action: f384-400: Chatter is already scribbling. It slaps on a second coral patch, then rolls Kern tighter so the scroll slims and stretches (sleeker = faster) and knots a coral headband onto it; a third chalk tally ticks on. f401-405: the whistle. f406-431: Kern goes round the loop in one speed-lined streak. The gate lamp blinks emerald and the bars flip open; the scale thunks level and Torchy nods. Each is held sharp for at least 4 frames inside the blur. Kern screeches to a stop at the start line.
beats.concept: Iterative refinement with evaluator feedback (AlphaEvolve-style retries, up to 5 attempts). Every new version is compiled and verified again before it is timed.
beats.camera: The whip lands close on the hands; then one continuous whip along the track with heavy smear, easing sharp at the gate and at the scale.
beats.transition_out: Continuous whip (speed-line smear) that decelerates exactly onto the start-line framing.

beats.shot: REMATCH -> Perf@1 > 1: a race dolly, then a low front 3/4 at the finish.
beats.action: f432-445: the Oracle winds its key, smug. Sleek Kern crouches low with slit eyes and fluttering headband tails. The crown clicks. f446-470: Kern rockets off in a huge stretch; hand-lettered 'ZOOM!' tears off behind it, and it overtakes. The Oracle's eyes pop and its key spins frantically as it pistons harder. f471-478: Kern crosses first under the Stopwatch Arch; both hands stop, the coral one before the gold one; a 2-frame impact frame. f479-527 (payoff): a coral-and-cream sunburst flat pops up behind the arch, and extruded 3D coral block letters reading 'Perf@1 > 1' slam onto the track at centre (squash, overshoot, shake). Kern leaps with star eyes at frame-left, clear of the letters, showing its 'Pass@1' stamp. At frame-right the Oracle does a take, then tips its laurel and offers a handshake. The hold is at least 1.4 s.
beats.concept: Perf@1 = oracle latency / kernel latency. Above 1 means the LLM-written kernel beats the hand-tuned oracle, and the kernel already carries its Pass@1 for correctness. Both headline metrics land at once.
beats.camera: A side dolly at race speed with speed lines. On the finish, a crash move to a low front 3/4, then a slow push-in (fov 30 -> 27) with an 8 % punch on the slam. The letters are centred in the card band.
beats.transition_out: Brush wipe driven by the story: Kern dashes off, and its fat coral speed streak smears across the whole frame like a brush stroke. Under full cover the camera moves to the coach's bench, and the streak clears as Kern skids in.

beats.shot: 164 + NAME -> NEXT SHEET: a low medium at the bench, tilting up the sheet stack.
beats.action: f528-548: Kern skids in beside Chatter and they high-five (both squash). Kern trots off frame-left with a towel over its shoulder. f549-590: Chatter turns for the next sheet, and the camera tilts up the towering stack (4 degree dutch). It has a thick cream band (Standard 139), a thin coral band with crinkled, oddly cut edges (OOD 13, novel operators) and a thin band edged in strange ink glyphs (DSL 12, new languages). Extruded 3D coral numerals reading '164' pop out of the stack's face (overshoot, settle) under the hand-painted 'TritonGym' gym sign. Chatter looks up the stack, eyes wide, mouth 'o', and gulps, then rolls its shoulders. f591-623: it plucks the top blank sheet, slaps it on the desk, wipes the chalk tallies with its elbow and raises the pencil. The camera tilts back down and settles into frame 0's pose.
beats.concept: The benchmark: 164 operators in three splits (139 Standard, 13 OOD, 12 DSL), each run through the same standard loop of compile, verify and profile. That is TritonGym.
beats.camera: A low medium and a modest tilt up that keeps '164' in rows ~380-700 and the sign at rows ~200-300, left of x = 1590. Hold about 1.2 s on '164', then tilt down and push to the f0 pose and velocity.
beats.transition_out: Seamless loop: a continuous move into frame 0 (Chatter, pencil raised over the new blank sheet).

proposals.payoff: Beat 7 (f479-527) is the payoff. After two failures (the CLANG at compile, then losing by a nose), the twice-patched, sleeker Kern outruns the hand-wound Oracle under the Stopwatch Arch. Extruded 3D coral block letters reading 'Perf@1 > 1' slam onto the track at centre over a sunburst, while Kern, already stamped 'Pass@1' by Torchy, leaps with star eyes and the Oracle tips its laurel. The frame says correct and faster than the hand-tuned oracle, both metrics earned by the loop. Beat 8 widens it to scale: this was one operator. A 3D '164' pops out of the stack of sheets still to write (bands in the true 139 / 13 / 12 proportions) under the 'TritonGym' sign, and the LLM takes the next sheet, so the loop restarts.
text_on_screen: CLANG! (hand-lettered SFX, beat 2: the compile gate rejects the kernel)
Pass@1 (emerald rubber-stamp print that Torchy stamps on Kern, beat 4; it stays on Kern)
ZOOM! (hand-lettered SFX, beat 7 rematch launch; the first word to drop if the lettering feels heavy)
Perf@1 > 1 (extruded 3D coral block letters, beat 7 payoff)
164 (extruded 3D coral numerals popping out of the sheet stack, beat 8)
TritonGym (hand-painted gym sign above the stack, beat 8; the only appearance of the name)
proposals.loop_seam: Frame 623 flows into frame 0 in one continuous camera move. The beat 8 tilt-down ends in the same slow push (fov about 32, 2 degree dutch, same drift velocity) that beat 1 starts with. Chatter's pencil-raise anticipation carries across the seam, and the blank sheet on the desk at f0 is the one it plucked at f591. The chalk tallies were wiped, so the board is clean at f0 and the first tally appears during the f6-40 scribble. Kern left frame-left at f548, so at f0 it does not exist yet. The gate (closed, lamp cream), the scale (empty left pan, Torchy on the right pan) and the Oracle (at the start line) all reset off-camera during beats 7-8. The stack's height is kept constant, so the missing sheet is invisible. The film is 624 frames at 24 fps; verify that the render hash of f624 equals f0.
proposals.poster_moment: Frame ~505, the beat 7 payoff hold, as a low front 3/4 at the finish line. The 3D coral block letters 'Perf@1 > 1' are centred in the card band over a coral-and-cream sunburst, with the giant Stopwatch Arch behind them on the emerald GPU-board track. At frame-left, sleek Kern is mid-leap with star eyes, showing its coral patches, headband and emerald 'Pass@1' stamp. At frame-right the Oracle is mid-take with its wind-up key spinning. Nobody overlaps the letters, and nothing sits in the top-right pill zone.
proposals.risks:
1. Pass@1 nuance: Pass@1 is strictly scored on the workflow's final kernel, but the stamp is given mid-loop. Beat 6 shows the refined kernel re-verified (the scale thunks level), so the stamp stays true. If the accuracy reviewer objects, move the stamp to beat 7, right after the finish line.
2. The speech balloon could read as a chat-UI icon. Keep it a heavy-inked, halftoned, bevelled 3D comic balloon with a curved spike foot and full squash-and-stretch acting, and never add typing dots.
3. The puns (torch = PyTorch, wind-up key = hand-tuned) may escape non-ML viewers. Their roles still read (a reference judge, a champion to beat). Add tiny labels ('PyTorch' on Torchy's handle, 'oracle' on the Oracle's sash) only if review demands it, since they count against the text budget.
4. The Oracle as a rival must not read as one model winning TritonGym. The Oracle is a kernel, not a model, and no model is named. The handshake and the '164, next sheet' ending frame the win as one operator's result.
5. Chatter must stay off the track during the races, so that speed reads as kernel speed, not LLM speed.
6. Density: 8 beats and 3 stations in 26 s. The beat 6 whip montage must stay legible (gate lamp and level scale each sharp for at least 4 frames). If it muddles, lengthen beat 6 to 2.5 s and trim beat 8's high-five.
7. The four named workflows (One-shot, Geak, AlphaEvolve, Leader) and the live leaderboard are deliberately not depicted; they are only implied by the failed first attempt and the iterative patches. This is a choice for clarity.
8. The OOD and DSL bands (13 and 12 sheets) are thin and their edge styles won't read at card size. That is acceptable, because '164' is the read.
9. The tall stack against a 2.1-2.6:1 card crop: keep the tilt modest and test the card crop on beat 8.
10. Production:
    - The scroll roll-up (bend deformer) and the crumple (mesh swap) are the trickiest rigs; hide the swaps under impact frames.
    - The flame must be flat cel with ink, never bloom.
    - The GPU board must use inked gold traces with halftone, never neon, or it drifts toward the 'AI glow' look.
    - The Stopwatch Arch is an object, but it echoes the Qubrio picture book's stopwatch Tick; keep it clearly a finish-line apparatus.
11. Text count is six items (CLANG!, ZOOM!, Pass@1, Perf@1 > 1, 164, TritonGym). Drop ZOOM! first if a lens says there is too much lettering.
12. Only 4 characters are used, plus acting apparatus, which is well under the cap. Crowds are not needed anywhere.

proposals.title: The Arena of 164
proposals.logline: In TritonGym, a GPU stadium crowned by a ring of 164 event lights, an LLM athlete writes a little Triton kernel. The kernel gets CLANGed at the same compile gate that stops a rival one-shot dart, is fixed in the agent loop, passes the weigh-in against the PyTorch reference and outruns the gold hand-tuned oracle. Then the camera pulls back: its win lights one bulb out of 164.

cast.name: Blurb
cast.concept: The LLM under test, the model athlete. An LLM writes text, so it is a talking speech balloon, and kernels pop out of its tail when it 'speaks'.
cast.design: An extruded, bevelled speech-balloon shape (a rounded ellipse with a pointed tail at bottom-left, about 1.3 units wide) in warm cream. An emerald torus sweatband runs across the crown. Capsule arms end in sphere mitts, and stubby capsule legs end in squashed-sphere emerald sneakers. The ink face is painted on the front: dot eyes by default, plus happy arcs, wide eyes, a squint and a think-up look. A mouth appears only on takes (cheeks puffed on the inhale, an O on the gulp), with a sweat-drop decal. Acting: it inflates (stretch) before it speaks, then squashes hard as a kernel pops out. This is the existing buildLLM in films/tritongym/tg_cast.js.
cast.silhouette: The widest, roundest shape in the film: a speech bubble on legs with a pointed tail. Nothing else is round and asymmetric.

cast.name: Tri
cast.concept: The Triton GPU kernel the LLM writes, the thing that gets compiled, verified and profiled.
cast.design: An emerald capsule body (r 0.3). A cream trident crest of three cones on a half-torus collar (Triton's trident). Capsule limbs with cream sphere mitts and ink-violet squashed-sphere shoes. Painted faces: determined slits, a teeth-grin when sprinting, spiral eyes after the CLANG, star eyes at the finish. After the loop it wears a small patch on its chest (a flattened rounded box with a stitched-edge decal), the visible trace of the refinement. This is the existing buildKernel.
cast.silhouette: A small upright pill topped by three spikes. It is the only spiky head, and the smallest hero.

cast.name: The Oracle
cast.concept: The hand-tuned oracle Triton kernel that every Standard operator comes with. It sets the speed to beat (Perf@1 = oracle latency / generated latency).
cast.design: buildKernel with oracle:true, scaled about 1.3x Tri and squatter (a wider capsule radius). Gold/ochre body, a laurel ring of 12 flattened leaf spheres, a coral torus sash worn diagonally, brown shoes. Smug half-lidded eyes that flip to wide and worried at the photo finish, then its laurel slips down over its eyes.
cast.silhouette: A bigger, broader pill whose outline is broken by a leafy ring and a diagonal sash. Next to little Tri it reads as 'champion'.

cast.name: Dash
cast.concept: A kernel from a rival one-shot team: a single pass, no retry, and a failure scores 0. It shows that the same standardised gate serves every workflow team.
cast.design: A coral dart laid horizontally: a cone nose, a cylinder-shaft body, three thin extruded-triangle fletching fins at the tail and two tiny capsule legs underneath. Dot eyes are painted on the shaft just behind the nose. It has no mouth except a wobble line when it droops. It quivers with boing lines when stuck.
cast.silhouette: The only horizontal character. It is an arrow, so it reads at a glance as 'a single shot'.

cast.name: The Gatekeeper
cast.concept: The standardised compile tool.
cast.design: Two chunky ink-violet box posts and a lintel box with a painted grumpy face (heavy brows and slit eyes; the mouth opens on the CLANG and to spit the error slip). Two lane portcullises of iron cylinder bars with cone tips drop and lift independently. This is the existing buildGate with its grate split into two lanes. The error slip is a curled thin plane with a coral X.
cast.silhouette: A doorway shaped like a capital pi, with a row of iron teeth.

cast.name: Torchy
cast.concept: The PyTorch reference that every kernel's output must match to within 0.01.
cast.design: An orange kettlebell (a sphere body with a torus handle) with a small flame on top made of two stacked cones, and tiny dot eyes on the bell. It sits on the left pan of the brass weigh-in scale, whose round dial has a thin emerald tolerance window. These are the existing buildKettlebell and buildScale.
cast.silhouette: A round bell with a loop handle and a lick of flame.

proposals.world:
The whole film is one continuous set: a GPU package built as a sports arena. The existing buildArena in films/tritongym/tg_world.js is the base.

**Ground and backdrop**
- The field is the lavender GPU die, with copper trace lines as lane markings, set in the ink-violet substrate on a huge emerald PCB slab.
- HBM stacks are the grandstands, left and right. Capacitor bollards run along the front edge.
- The back wall is a heat-sink fin wall with two slowly turning fans (constant life in the background). It fades into cream paper mist with distance.

**The one scale object: the HALO**
- A thick torus truss hangs on four cables above the die. It carries 164 fat marquee-bulb spheres (instanced, not a crowd of props).
- The bulbs form one continuous run of 139 emerald, then 13 coral, then 12 ink-violet, with a small gap between runs.
- A hand-lettered enamel TRITONGYM nameplate hangs on two chains from the front span, placed left of centre.
- Rule: the halo is never shot top-down, so it can never read as a donut chart. It is always seen low or oblique, as a stadium crown.

**The scoreboard drum**
- A chunky inked cylinder hangs on cables at the halo's centre, directly above the finish tape.
- It has two domed stadium lamps with painted plates reading 'Pass@1' and 'Perf@1'. The Perf@1 lamp has a physical flip-flap.
- A vertical brass rail holds four round portrait tokens. These are anonymous balloon faces in periwinkle, ochre, coral and cream; the cream one is Blurb.

**Three zones on the die, sized by their real proportions**
- STANDARD (139): the huge emerald-washed field over the back-left three-quarters of the die. It holds only three different apparatus, spaced out and fading into the mist:
  - a matmul barbell with grid-faced plates
  - a flat-then-rising activation ramp
  - a quantization staircase
- OOD (13): a small sunken pit at back-right, lit coral. It holds one never-seen obstacle: a TorusKnot hurdle that slowly writhes and re-knots.
- DSL (12): a small sunken pit at front-right, lit violet. Its barbell has the same shape as the Standard one, but its two pennants read 'Gluon' and 'TLX'.

**The tool hub (front-centre, where every event is tested)**
- Blurb's start mark leads to the two-lane compile gate.
- A curved return lane (the agent loop) is painted on the die from the gate back to the start mark.
- Next come the brass weigh-in scale, then two-lane start blocks for a short sprint.
- The sprint ends at a finish tape beside a stopwatch on a pole, under the drum.

**Palette and look**
- Palette: warm cream paper, emerald #059669 dominant, coral #ef4b5f as the single pop, ink-violet for shadows and ink, brass for metal.
- NPR look matches reference/style-comic: two-step cel, halftone in the terminator, boiling ink, off-register colour, paper grain.
- Coloured light is shown as hard-edged inked cones with halftone, never bloom.
- Scale is shown by ONE ring of lights, three differently sized zones and a camera that travels. It is never shown by rows of identical props. Object count stays in the tens, plus the 164 instanced bulbs.

beats.shot: B1 THE ARENA OF 164. An iris opens on an extreme close-up of one lit emerald bulb on the halo. The camera pulls back along the ring's curve, then cranes down through the ring to the hub.
beats.action: f0-5: the iris opens on the lit bulb. f6-45: the bulb fires a chase. The long emerald run fills bulb by bulb (f6-29), then the short coral run (f30-37), then the short violet run (f38-45). As each run lights, it drops a hard-edged inked light cone onto its own zone: the vast emerald field, the little coral pit, the little violet pit. f24-55: the TRITONGYM enamel nameplate swings through the foreground on its chains, creaking, large and left of centre. f46-83: the ring lights fade back-to-front (house lights down) as the camera cranes down through the ring. Blurb, small at the hub, is warming up (arm circles, then a squat with squash). It looks up at the ring and gives a little awed bounce.
beats.concept: TritonGym is the benchmark, shown as an arena built on a GPU (die field, HBM grandstands, heat-sink wall). The ring of 164 bulbs is the 164 operators. The three runs, sized 139/13/12, are the three splits: Standard, OOD and DSL. The project name appears once, as an object label.
beats.camera: Iris-out, then a dolly back along the ring with a slight dutch, then a descending crane that tilts down. It never stops. The nameplate passes within rows 190-600, left of x 1500.
beats.transition_out: Continuous camera move: the crane lands at Blurb's chest height and becomes the orbit of B2.

beats.shot: B2 THREE ZONES. An over-the-shoulder orbit around Blurb at the hub, with three eased stops linked by two short orbit-whips.
beats.action: f84-111 STANDARD: behind Blurb, looking out over the vast emerald field. The matmul barbell, the activation ramp and the quantization staircase recede into the mist; the field feels endless. Blurb nods, confident, and gives a mitt thumbs-up. f112-119: the orbit whips right with smear. f120-147 OOD: the small coral pit, where the TorusKnot hurdle writhes and re-knots itself. Blurb double-takes (stretch up, eyes wide) and an inked '?' pops over it. f148-153: another orbit-whip. f154-179 DSL: the small violet pit, with the familiar barbell under flapping pennants reading 'Gluon' and 'TLX'. Blurb tilts its whole balloon sideways, squints and scratches with a mitt, then snaps upright, determined, and turns toward the hub.

beats.camera: An orbit at chest height around Blurb. Blurb is always frame-left in the lower half, and the zone is the right two-thirds of the frame. The zone reads large and deep for Standard, and small and close for the two pits.
beats.transition_out: Whip pan with smear, from the DSL pit back past Blurb to the start mark facing the compile gate (B3).

beats.shot: B3 WRITE. A low three-quarter medium on Blurb at the start mark. The Gatekeeper's arch sits small in the background, screen-right.
beats.action: f180-195: Blurb inhales. The balloon body inflates and stretches up, cheeks puff and eyes shut (anticipation). f196-203: Blurb 'speaks'. It squashes down hard and Tri pops out of the balloon's tail like a gumball, stretched in mid-air. f204-215: Tri lands in a sprinter's crouch; its crest boings and its face sets to determined. f216-227: Blurb points a mitt at the gate, and Tri digs its feet in.
beats.concept: The LLM generates a Triton kernel. The model under test writes the code that TritonGym will judge.
beats.camera: A slight push-in during the inhale, then a quick tilt that follows Tri's arc. Both faces stay in rows 300-800.
beats.transition_out: Whip pan right: the camera launches with Tri toward the compile gate (continuous).

beats.shot: B4 CLANG, AND AGAIN. A side-on tracking dolly at runner height into the two-lane compile gate. Whips follow Tri back along the painted loop lane and out again.
beats.action: f228-245: Tri sprints for the gate. Dash, the rival team's coral dart, streaks in on the parallel lane from screen-right-back with speed lines. f246-251: the Gatekeeper's brows slam down, both portcullises drop, and CLANG! is lettered on a diagonal left of the gate. There are two posterised impact frames. Dash thunks point-first into the bars and sticks there, quivering. Tri smacks the bars, squashes flat, slides down and shows spiral eyes. f252-275: the Gatekeeper spits a curled slip with a coral X. Tri snatches it and boomerangs back along the curved loop lane to Blurb. Blurb reads it (think-up eyes), puffs, and pops a small patch onto Tri's chest. f276-311: Tri whips back along the loop. Only Tri's portcullis grumbles up, and Tri zips under it past Dash. Dash is still stuck on its lane and droops, with a wobble mouth: one shot, no retry. f312-323: the camera stays with Tri as it heads for the scale.

beats.camera: A tracking dolly with a 3-frame impact shake on the CLANG. Then a whip pan left along the loop with smear, a short beat on Blurb, a whip pan right back through the gate and a continuous track past Dash. The CLANG lettering sits in rows 220-520, never over a face.
beats.transition_out: Continuous camera move: the track carries Tri through the raised portcullis and straight onto the weigh-in pan (B5).

beats.shot: B5 WEIGH-IN. A frontal medium on the brass balance scale, with Torchy on the left pan and the round dial centred on the post.
beats.action: f324-335: Tri leaps onto the right pan. The beam lurches and Torchy bounces. f336-359: the needle swings wide past the thin emerald window, one way and then the other. Tri bites its lip and Torchy's flame leans with the swing (tension). f360-371: the needle settles inside the window with a tiny overshoot. f372-383: the bell on top rings, lettered DING!. Torchy's flame puffs up happily and Tri pumps a fist.

beats.camera: A slow push-in toward the dial, so the needle and the narrow window read big at card size. The dial ends centred at about x 960, y 470.
beats.transition_out: Match cut: the round dial with its needle upright becomes the round stopwatch face with its hand at twelve, at the same size and screen position (B6).

beats.shot: B6 THE ORACLE RACE. It opens on the stopwatch face and pulls back to the finish pole. Then a low side-tracking dolly runs along two lanes of copper die traces toward the tape.
beats.action: f384-395: the stopwatch hand clicks. As the camera pulls back, the Oracle, big, gold and laurelled, stretches smugly in the inside lane, with Tri beside it, patch on its chest. f396-407: set: both crouch (anticipation). Go: both stretch off the blocks. f408-443: the Oracle leads by a head and glances back smugly. Tri grits its teeth, its legs blur into a smear-wheel, and it closes the gap. f444-467: photo finish. Tri's trident crest breaks the tape a hair first, and the stopwatch hand stops. The Oracle's eyes go wide and its laurel slips down over them.
beats.concept: The profile tool and Perf@1 = oracle Triton latency / generated latency. Finishing ahead of the hand-tuned oracle means Perf@1 > 1. The race runs on the GPU die.
beats.camera: A match-cut pull-back, then a low tracking dolly at runner height that stays level with the two heads. A crash zoom lands on the tape at the finish, with the tape in rows 350-650.
beats.transition_out: Continuous camera move: a crash tilt up from the snapped tape to the scoreboard drum hanging just above (B7).

beats.shot: B7 THE LIVE BOARD. A low-angle medium with a slight dutch on the hanging scoreboard drum, which is still swaying on its cables.
beats.action: f468-479: the drum sways from the tilt's arrival, and the 'Pass@1' lamp thunks on, emerald, with a check mark. f480-495: the 'Perf@1' flap flips over to show a coral '> 1', with backOut overshoot and a wobble. f496-527: on the brass rail, Blurb's portrait token hops up one slot. It swaps with a periwinkle token that squeaks aside, surprised. Blurb moves up a place, not to the top.
beats.concept: The live leaderboard ranks models by Pass@1 and Perf@1. A generic climb is shown, and no model is shown winning TritonGym.
beats.camera: The tilt settles with an overshoot, pushes in slightly on the two lamps, then drifts to the rail. The drum stays centre-left, below y 130 and left of x 1500, clear of the LIVE pill.
beats.transition_out: Continuous camera move: a pull-back that cranes down to field level behind Blurb and Tri, with the halo rising into frame (B8).

beats.shot: B8 ONE OF 164. A low three-quarter view from the field. Blurb and Tri are in the lower-left foreground, and the halo arcs across the upper third with the TRITONGYM nameplate upper-left.
beats.action: f528-543: Blurb hoists Tri overhead, celebrating. One emerald bulb on the near arc pings on, with a squash-pop and a small inked ray burst. f544-559: the camera widens to show the whole ring, with 163 bulbs still dark: a long emerald run, then a short coral run, then a short violet run. Extruded block numerals '164' slam up into the space inside the ring, with backOut overshoot, a wobble and a hatched cast shadow. f560-587 (hold): Blurb's grin freezes. Its eyes go from happy to wide, a sweat drop appears, and it gulps (O mouth). Tri shrugs, grins, and grabs Blurb's mitt. f588-611: they jog off toward the zones, frame-left. The camera pushes up past the numerals toward the lit bulb. f612-623: the iris closes on the bulb.
